## 1. GLSS 5 sampled 8,687 households in 580 areas over 2005/06

- Nationally representative survey, about one year of fieldwork
- 8,687 households, 36,500 usual members, 580 enumeration areas (13–15 households each)
- Weighted: 5.5 million households, 22.2 million persons
- Policy context: *(add the 2005/06 poverty-reduction context from GSS 2007)*

## 2. Welfare is built in three steps, from spending to adult equivalents

Nominal consumption → price deflator (region, locality, month) → adult equivalents

- Included: food, imputed food, other and imputed non-food spending
- Rent, durables, vehicles, health, ceremonies: *(confirm against our file)*
- Units: old cedis, ¢10,000 = GH¢1

## 3. Poverty lines price a 2,900 kcal food basket plus non-food needs

- Old method (2006 prices): upper GH¢370.89, extreme GH¢288.47
- New method: GLSS 6 lines, welfare deflated to 2012/13 prices
- Lines are per adult equivalent per year

## 4. Person weights and the survey design change the answer

- PSUs: 580 clusters; weight = household weight × household size
- Poverty is a share of **persons**, not households
- Strata: *(to confirm)*
